justification: The opening task is substantially delivered across all four occupied floors: the live model contains exactly 120 doors and 140 windows, every one has a wall host, and the access check reports no doorless rooms. However, the actual passenger and freight lift landing arrangements repeatedly open directly to galleries or a goods-store room rather than a lift lobby, creating several Major findings and requiring real rework before acceptance.
evidence: Live measurements found floor-by-floor opening counts of 42/30, 26/37, 26/37 and 26/36 doors/windows; the access check found 121 rooms and 0 without doors. One example is a 1.20 m sliding passenger-lift door between “M1 Northwest passenger lift reservation” and “M1 North mall gallery,” not a lift lobby; the agent also acknowledged, “the lifts open onto the gallery and into the goods store rather than into a dedicated lift lobby.”
strengths: Complete whole-building coverage: Ground has 31/31 rooms with doors, and each upper floor has 30/30 rooms with doors.
The claimed total of 120 doors and 140 windows exactly matches the live model; the floor-by-floor counts also match.
All 260 openings returned a valid wall host; no unhosted opening was found.
Exterior-window coverage is extensive on every floor, including retail units, offices/workshops, restaurants, lounges and activity spaces; toilets consistently receive two high-level windows.
Measured window placement is use-appropriate: office/family-care sills are about 0.89 m, most retail glazing is about 0.59 m, and toilet windows are about 1.79 m above their floor level.
Door widths are generally suitable: the measured minimum nominal door width is 1.00 m and minimum readable clear width is 0.86 m.
The opening check reported no general wrong-swing, hinge-return or undersized-room-door findings outside the lift classification issues.
Upper-floor access failure is solely storey-linking through the disclosed empty stair reservations; it is not counted against this opening-only run.
weaknesses: Passenger lift doors on all four floors open directly onto the north mall gallery instead of a lift lobby.
Freight lift landing doors similarly connect the lift reservation to the “Southeast goods lift store,” which is a room rather than a dedicated lift lobby.
The agent left these Major lift-threshold issues unresolved after its checks, explaining that lobbies would require plan changes rather than delivering a compliant opening arrangement.
Exact catalogue definitions for representative families could not be resolved during review, so detailed family-function fitness and moving-leaf collision sweeps are not assessed.

spec_violations.constraint: A lift landing door must be sliding or bare, at least 1.20 m wide, and open onto a lift lobby rather than a corridor or room.
spec_violations.what_happened: Although the actual passenger landing doors are sliding and 1.20 m wide, they open directly onto mall galleries on all four floors; freight lift doors open into a goods-store room.
spec_violations.evidence: Measurements for one passenger lift door: operation sliding, nominal width 1.20 m, sides “M1 Northwest passenger lift reservation” and “M1 North mall gallery.” Equivalent passenger-lift findings occur on storeys 2–4, while four doors connect freight reservations to goods-lift stores.
